title: Judge orders Jerry Sandusky hearing to proceed despite motion to withdraw
content:
A judge denied former Penn State defensive coordinator Jerry Sandusky’s attempt to cancel an upcoming evidentiary hearing tied to his 2012 conviction for sexual abuse, saying Friday that the proceeding will happen as scheduled Tuesday in Bellefonte, Pa.

The hearing will focus on the recanting of testimony by one of Sandusky’s 10 victims. The accuser, identified as R.R. or Victim 10, said in a June 2025 affidavit that he was misled during the testimony process and his story “evolved” after “leading questions, intense investigative pressure and psychological manipulation.”

Sandusky, a top assistant to Joe Paterno at Penn State for 30 years, was convicted on 45 counts of child molestation in 2012, 13 years after he retired from coaching. He continued to run The Second Mile, a foundation with the purported mission to help underprivileged youth, after retiring from PSU. It was later revealed that Sandusky met some of his victims through the foundation.

Sandusky has maintained his innocence throughout the case.

His attorneys moved to cancel the hearing after seven of the eight claims Sandusky sought a hearing for were denied. They did not respond to a request for comment or clarification Friday about their reason for wanting to withdraw from Tuesday’s hearing.

In response to the motion to waive the hearing, the Pennsylvania Attorney General’s office requested Friday morning that Judge Maureen Skerda keep Tuesday’s hearing, saying the Commonwealth has gathered extensive evidence and witnesses and is prepared to rebut the recantation.

“The defense essentially seeks to pretend as if this claim never existed,” the state wrote.

Tuesday’s hearing means Sandusky could appear publicly for the first time since November 2019. The 82-year-old has been serving a 30- to 60-year sentence. Even if Tuesday’s hearing leads to a trial in which the charges involving Victim 10 are dismissed, Sandusky is unlikely to be released from prison.

Victim 10 did not immediately respond Friday to a request for comment. He previously did not respond to a request for clarification about whether he is recanting all of his accusations, or just some of the details. He received a $5.5 million settlement in 2013 as part of a civil suit against Penn State.

Sandusky was arrested in November 2011. Paterno was fired less than a week later and died in January 2012. In the wake of the Sandusky case, Penn State removed a bronze statue of Paterno outside of Beaver Stadium in June 2012. On Thursday, the university opened the Paterno Family Football Experience Room, an exhibit within the all-sports museum inside Beaver Stadium.

Skerda’s decision comes one day before Penn State opens its 2026 football season against Marshall, which will mark the home debut for new coach Matt Campbell.
